subject: Atlanta Fed GDPNow (GDP nowcast, US)
headline: Beats the no-change null by a wide margin (75% lower MAE) on 37 quarters of real-time vintages — qualified because that skill is measured against the advance estimate, not the settled number.

findings.question: Is the forecast a model at all, or an accounting identity?
findings.answer: Bridge-equation nowcast; beats the no-change null on MAE by 75% (1.26 vs 5.05 pp)

findings.question: Does it beat the null out of sample?
findings.answer: 28 of 37 quarters, MAE ratio 0.25 (<1 = beats the null)

findings.question: Is that skill against the FIRST publication or the settled number?
findings.answer: Target matters: skill against the advance estimate is not skill against the number that survives revision. Both are reported.

findings.question: Are the inputs real-time vintages, or revised history?
findings.answer: Real-time vintages (ALFRED) throughout; a vintage that post-dates the forecast is refused by guard_nowcast_predates_release

findings.question: Can the evaluation go red?
findings.answer: Four guards, each mutation-proved: vintage ordering, shared benchmark vintage, first-publication target, units

limitations: Skill is measured against the first publication; against the final number the nowcast's advantage narrows and is not established here.
The evaluation uses one public dataset and one target definition; neither has been independently replicated outside this repository.
